title: North Carolina's 5th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for North Carolina's 5th Congressional District pits 10-term Republican incumbent Virginia Foxx against Democratic nominee Chuck Hubbard in a rematch from 2024. The district, which covers northwestern North Carolina from the Appalachian Mountains to the northern suburbs of Greensboro, has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+9 and backed Donald Trump by 18 points in 2024, making it a reliably Republican seat. Foxx, who chairs the House Rules Committee, is seeking an 11th term on a platform of conservative fiscal policy and limited government, while Hubbard, a former local journalist, is running on a platform of supporting working families, public education, and affordable healthcare. North Carolina redrew its congressional district boundaries in October 2025 ahead of this election.
polling_note: No public general election polls were found for this race as of mid-2026.

candidates.name: Virginia Foxx
candidates.summary: Virginia Foxx is the incumbent U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2004. She serves as Chairwoman of the House Committee on Rules and previously chaired the Committee on Education and the Workforce, and is consistently ranked among the most conservative members of Congress. Prior to her congressional service, she spent 10 years in the North Carolina Senate and held various roles in higher education, including president of Mayland Community College.

candidates.name: Chuck Hubbard
candidates.summary: Chuck Hubbard is a Democratic candidate challenging incumbent Virginia Foxx for North Carolina's 5th Congressional District. A native of Wilkes County, he spent 40 years as a journalist at the Wilkes Journal-Patriot, a newspaper founded by his grandfather in 1932. In 2022, he ran unsuccessfully for the North Carolina House of Representatives, and he previously faced Foxx in the 2024 general election.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling exists for this race (0 polls as of mid-2026), which reduces confidence and means the forecast relies on structural factors rather than direct voter-intent data. The district has a Cook PVI of R+9 and backed Trump by 18 points in 2024, placing it among the more Republican-leaning seats nationally. Incumbent Virginia Foxx is seeking an 11th term and chairs the House Rules Committee, a powerful institutional position. Her opponent, Chuck Hubbard, is a repeat challenger who previously lost to Foxx in 2024 and also ran unsuccessfully for a state legislative seat in 2022. The district was redrawn in October 2025, which introduces some redistricting uncertainty, though the structural partisan lean of the area (northwestern NC, from the Appalachians to Greensboro suburbs) has been consistently Republican. Given the incumbency advantage, committee chair status, district partisanship, and lack of competitive historical signal in this district, Republicans hold an overwhelming advantage consistent with a safe_r rating (~95%+ win probability).
